caption: The drawing depicts two bags, each with a strap, drawn in colored pencil or crayon on a tan background. The upper bag has a wide, rounded body with a red and pink color scheme, further accentuated by blue, green, and purple details, with visible floral or leaf motifs. The edge of the opening is trimmed with a darker color, and the strap is depicted in a deep red, with a knot and a hanging tassel at the top. The lower bag has a more oval shape and is primarily green with a textured, beaded pattern; it also features accents in darker green, brown, and patches of purple. The opening of this bag is lined with a pink or red border, and the strap is long and dark brown. Handwritten text appears to the right of each bag, identifying the artist as M. Knapp, noting the date as November 25, 1925, and describing both as “Eastern Woodland” bags from case 2E, with the top labeled as a “Wooden Bag” and the lower as a “Beaded Bag.”
title: Beaded Bags
